topic: The Mars Climate Orbiter unit mix-up of 1999
title: The Unit Mix-Up That Lost A Spacecraft #siliconverdict #space #techfails
description: In 1999 a mix-up between pound-force and newton units cost NASA the Mars Climate Orbiter, a lesson in checking interfaces.
pinned_comment: Software or people? Reply with one word.

scenes.narration: One unit mix-up destroyed a spacecraft and roughly a hundred million dollars.
Stay to the end, because the bug was hiding in plain sight.
NASA launched the orbiter in 1998, and lost it near Mars the next year.
One team's software reported thrust in pound-force seconds, while navigation expected newton-seconds.
The two units differ by a factor of about four point four five.
Each small thrust error added up over months, pushing the craft off course.
The loss cost roughly 125 million dollars, ended by a single assumption.
The math was right on both sides. The mistake lived in the handoff between them.
The review board urged clearer unit checks between teams after the loss.
The lesson is simple: a number without a unit is only half a number.
Follow for more tech. Was it a software bug, or a people problem?
